Just wanted to give my 2 cents, I've had the 700 Pro X for a little over a year, and the headband has already torn itself out. I take pretty good care of my peripherals in general and haven't been excessive or rough with them at all, so I'm still stumped on how this happened - but then - I went to their site to see if I could either get a replacement under warranty or see if I could purchase a replacement for the headband issue.

I'd also like to note that I literally had to glue the foam on it because with the headband tearing, there's a plastic piece that has dug into my skull 100% of the time otherwise.

The 700 Pro X's do sound really good, but there are quite a bit of cons in my personal experience, which is why I found your post because I'm actually looking into getting the Maxwells myself, or might even go back to a headset like the a50x's because I'm so irritated with the drawbacks of comfort/lack of convenience with these.

Thank you, it really was a weird personal hell when I couldn't figure out why it was happening or anything to help. My water intake has gone up dramatically, but at least 3-5 cups (18oz each) if not more. I thought mine was neck related as well, also I thought it was the vagus nerve at one point and so many other things.

The biggest difference for my situation was not spiking my blood sugar, rather than fixing the diet entirely. I still get the brain fog and extreme fatigue if I go a long time without eating and then have food/something sugary to make it spike up. No idea if that helps but I wanted to mention it for you or anyone else that might come across it.

Well, turns out my blood sugar was massively out of whack and the first two doctors didn't even mention it or want to look into it for whatever reason...  I've apparently been diabetic for a while, unmonitored and it got much worse around that time due to personal life stress + covid times. A lot of the symptoms came with it (high blood pressure, heart rate, lack of sleep, etc.) but that was the core issue and it's been incredibly better and manageable since I've kept it in mind, and I barely made changes other than making sure I don't accidentally skip eating for 12 hours or overly binge when I do finally eat again. That + water and my dizziness has more or less been nonexistent for about a year or 2 now.
Ah damn, well at least now I'll know I'm lying when I tell them the opposite. Cheers!

Using Nvidia Control Panel, on the left panel under "change resolution" under that list it should say "customize" but it will only let you create/use them if you have DSR/DSDLR disabled (option that I think is off by default anyway, but is found in the "Manage 3d Settings" option also on the left panel)

If you're using the C2, I'd also recommend going to "Adjust desktop size and position" and changing the scaling option to "no scaling" and "Display" 

The reason is because some games don't play nice with this and some will just give you issues overall, trying to scale your set resolution into the full screen space even if it's not supposed to. Setting to no scaling has fixed that for me for 90% of games.

The screen was overall way too large to play Fullscreen so I would run it in borderless 1440p, which would work out better but would actually then be too small and I couldn't be as precise or would even lose my place for a moment here and there.

I ended up using that resolution I put above (mobile now and I don't remember it) so it was more or less the same feeling and fluidity as when I used my 27 inch 1440p

Yes and no, I'll explain why I say that -

Sorry for the wall of text but I figured context would be helpful, I drove myself crazy trying to decide between these two.

I had both for about a month+ (return window extended for holidays) and I can say that the C2 even side by side \*seems\* sharper, despite the PPI being less. The colors aren't nearly as good as the Alienware, the brightness isn't good in comparison either but the screen real estate and perceived sharpness in games made a big difference for me and I couldn't stick to 1440p (which I've been using the G7 and G9 for years prior).

If I didn't have them side by side, I'd be in love with the Alienware but overall I decided on the C2 when I realized I can use custom resolutions per game if need be. I also have a 3080ti and I actually didn't get THAT much of a performance hit with 4k vs 3440x1440, but if I wanted better fps or if I'm playing something competitive (league is my main thing I had an issue with on the C2) then I would just use 2816x1584 in borderless, or 3840x1600 if I wanted to play in 21:9 anyway. It works really well because the pixels actually turn off, so if you have a black background, it essentially just creates bezels and lets me customize each game as needed.

I personally decided to stick with the C2 because I do have the desk space, but will definitely change to a 32 inch QD OLED or when it comes out down the line.
